To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that

1) mGlu receptors in the inferior colliculi of the GEP rat are involved in seizure generation; 2) mGlu receptor agonists can be used for the development of new antiepileptic drugs; and 3) the mGlu receptors of the inferior collicular complex of the GEP rats can be used as a novel animal model for the development of anticonvulsants.

activation of metabotropic glutamate receptors in inferior collicular neurons produces an immediate and transient (less than 10 minutes) proconvulsan effect followed by a delayed anticonvulsan effect lasting for more than 1 day.
